title: Kernel-checked results on the Riemann Hypothesis: de Bruijn-Newman bounds and a conditional Riemann-Roch-square criterion
description: Lean 4 formalizations, papers and a vendored copy of the Telperion certificate engine, collecting kernel-checked results around the Riemann Hypothesis. The Riemann Hypothesis is open and is not proved here. Unconditional: 0 <= Lambda <= 0.2811857 for the de Bruijn-Newman constant (dbn_newman along Dobner's proof, selberg_newman and selberg_newman_sharp for the extended Selberg class, dbn_real_zeros_of_qrh_unconditional from OpenAI's quasi-Riemann hypothesis, dbn_real_zeros_ge_2811857 from Baiying Liu's half-plane), each judged by Comparator with nanoda; pole-free one-prime Weil positivity for test functions supported in [-0.5493, 0.5493] (Hodge1.weil_positivity_poleFree2_window5493). Equivalences and conditional results: RH iff Weil positivity on pole-free tests (RvMBridgePF.rh_iff_poleFree_weil_positivity); RH iff that positivity for tests not supported in the window (Hodge1.rh_iff_poleFree2_outside_window5493); and the Riemann-Roch-square criterion: a family of RR-square windows covering every pole-free test implies RH (RvMBridgePF.rh_of_rr_windows), and conversely RH gives such windows trivially (RvMBridgePF.rh_iff_exists_rr_windows), so all content is a construction without reference to the zeros, together with the abstract Hodge-index theorems, a countermodel and function-field instances. No RR-square family is constructed. All theorems depend only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. OpenAI's and Liu's code is fetched at pinned commits and not redistributed. Not refereed. v1.0.2 re-syncs the Telperion copy to fix two engine defects found by an independent AI audit: winding-number zero counts are now rigorous segment enclosures (earlier ones were node-sampled), which adds a fifth off-line zero of the Davenport-Heilbronn function below height 300, and the Baez-Duarte emitter now uses Bagchi's family; no theorem in the papers or the progress record depended on either (see CHANGELOG.md).
